region: Cairo, Siwa Oasis and Upper Egypt
title: Egypt — Pyramids, an Oracle Oasis and the Theban Tombs
subtitle: From the first stone pyramids to Siwa's mud-salt town and the New Kingdom necropolis
summary: Thirteen days linking Saqqara and Islamic Cairo, a night bus to Siwa Oasis with three nights in town, and the temples and tombs of Luxor. Security is conditional because the Western Desert advice diverges.
introduction: The route follows Egyptian history from its oldest stone architecture to its last pagan oracle. In Cairo you walk Al-Muizz Street and spend a day among the Saqqara and Dahshur pyramids with a driver. A night bus along the Mediterranean road takes you to Siwa, where the Shali fortress rises from salt and the Oracle temple looks over date palms; days are spent on bicycles among the gardens, salt lakes and craft workshops. A flight south brings the columned halls of Karnak, the painted royal tombs of the Valley of the Kings and the quieter temples of Dendera and Abydos, before a sleeper train returns to Cairo.

exceptional.vsOman: Oman was a self-drive 4x4 and tent trip; this route is driver-, bus-, train- and guide-based because self-drive is inappropriate in Egypt, and no camping is included.
exceptional.vsPackageTourism: No Nile cruise or pyramids-only coach tour: Siwa, Saqqara/Dahshur, Dendera and Abydos are reached independently by public transport and small hired vehicles, with markets and local food at the centre.
exceptional.vsPortfolio: Egypt combines the oldest pyramids, a Siwi oasis with an Alexander-era oracle and Thebes in one route, a combination none of the other nineteen destinations offers; Jordan and Saudi Arabia have desert and Nabataean sites but not Pharaonic Egypt.

duration.note: Day 1 outbound and Day 13 return; two overnight bus legs and one sleeper train.

recommendedTravelWindow.rationale: After Eid al-Fitr (about 9–11 March) so shops and restaurants are open and domestic Eid travel has passed; warmer desert nights than February, but khamsin dust storms are possible and Luxor is hot at midday.

februarySuitability.summary: Pleasant Cairo and Luxor days and quiet sites, but it overlaps Ramadan (about 8 Feb – 9 Mar): shorter hours, daytime restaurant closures outside tourist areas, tired drivers, and cool nights in Siwa.

marchSuitability.summary: Mild to warm days, little rain; Eid al-Fitr falls at the start, so the second half of March is best. Risks are khamsin dust and heat in Luxor.

security.summary: Conditional. Re-read on 27 Nov 2026: FCDO and the Netherlands except only the oasis town of Siwa (and its access road) from their all-but-essential/orange Western Desert advice, France rates the Siwa oasis zone yellow but the surrounding desert orange or red, and the US asks travellers to reconsider travel to the Western and Libyan Deserts (Level 3). The former 4x4 dunes camp was removed (v1.1.0): the plan now stays inside Siwa town, its gardens and lakes. Siwa remains conditional because the US and European advice conflict.
security.assessedRoute: Cairo, Saqqara, Dahshur, Giza; Cairo–Alexandria–Marsa Matruh–Siwa road (bus); Siwa town and its immediate gardens and lakes only (three nights in town, no desert excursions or camps); Cairo–Luxor by air; Luxor West Bank, Dendera, Abydos; Luxor–Cairo by rail. Not assessed or included: any desert outside Siwa town, Bahariya, White and Black Deserts, Farafra, Dakhla, Kharga, Bahariya–Siwa road, Sinai, Red Sea coast.

conflictRisk.note: Egypt borders Libya, Sudan and Gaza; armed forces and criminal gangs are reported in the Western Desert near Libya; north Sinai is outside the route; Gaza and Sudan spillover raise regional tension but not on the route.

terrorismRisk.note: FCDO says attacks are likely to be attempted (security forces, religious sites); France calls the threat permanent and diffuse though the last Cairo attacks date to 2018-19.

kidnappingRisk.note: France states infiltration from Libya with kidnapping risk is 'not excluded' in the western border zone; Siwa lies about 50 km from that border.

regionalRestrictions: Do not travel within 20 km of the Libyan border or south of Siwa; do not leave Siwa town and its immediate gardens and lakes.
Bahariya–Siwa road is closed to tourists with military checkpoints (FCDO).
Expect police checkpoints and registration on the Siwa road.
ordinaryRisks: Road traffic: serious accidents are common; avoid night driving outside cities (France, FCDO) — the night buses are a trade-off.
Petty theft and scams around tourist sites; touting.
Heat, dust and khamsin storms in March; cold desert nights in February.
Food and water hygiene; stomach illness is common.
security.medicalAccess: Cairo and Luxor have private hospitals with international-standard care; Siwa has only a basic hospital and clinic.
security.insuranceConsiderations: Many policies exclude regions under FCDO 'all but essential' advice; confirm the policy explicitly covers Siwa and overnight bus travel, and medical repatriation.
security.reassessmentRequired: Re-check all five advisories before booking and two weeks before departure, especially the Western Desert wording, the Siwa colour on the French map, the Smartraveller Bahariya statement, Ramadan/Eid logistics, and Libya or Gaza escalation. If Siwa becomes red, orange or all-but-essential on any list, switch to the Cairo–Fayoum–Luxor–Aswan variant. Before reassessment, the dunes camp must be removed from the plan (A09/A00); reconsider eligibility only if the US lifts its Level 3 for the Western Desert.
